articles.title: Can Netanyahu stage a comeback in Israel? What if Eisenkot fails to form government
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, has been given the first opportunity to form the next government after President Isaac Herzog invited him
articles.body: Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, has been given the first opportunity to form the next government after President Isaac Herzog invited him on Saturday. The inconclusive October 27 election failed to give any party a clear parliamentary majority.However, with his coalition falling short of the numbers needed to govern, Eisenkot faces several challenges.He has options laid out to form a minority government. He can secure support from Arab parties, reach an understanding with ultra-Orthodox factions or explore a broader unity arrangement.But if he fails within the 42-day deadline, the incumbent Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could get another chance to form a government.Eisenkot's Yashar party and its potential allies have 48 seats in the 120-member parliament.While his seats fall short of the 61-seat majority mark required, support from Israel's two Arab parties, which together hold 19 seats, could help his bloc reach 67. The parties could support his government from outside without formally joining the coalition, allowing Eisenkot to attempt a minority government.How Eisenkot can form a minority governmentOne possibility is for Eisenkot to bring together his natural allies, including the centre-right Together party, The Democrats and Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing Israel Our Home. Their combined strength stands at 48 seats.The two Arab parties, Ra'am and the Joint List, could then provide outside support. Both have endorsed Eisenkot to form the next government and expressed willingness to work with his broader camp to prevent Netanyahu's return to power.However, this arrangement faces political hurdles. Eisenkot had pledged during his campaign not to include Arab parties in his government. Reversing that position could prove difficult, particularly after the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack hardened attitudes towards Israel's Arab minority.Lieberman has also repeatedly ruled out forming a minority government with Arab parties. So far, only The Democrats, a centre-left party, have publicly supported their inclusion.Netanyahu has also focused his campaign on delegitimising any government that relies on Arab support.There is a precedent for such an arrangement. Ra'am joined former prime minister Naftali Bennett's government in 2021. Bennett, who now heads the Together party, is among Eisenkot's potential partners. However, that government collapsed after 18 months, partly because of disagreements over the occupied West Bank.Can ultra-Orthodox parties give Eisenkot a majorityAnother option is to seek support from Israel's two ultra-Orthodox parties, which together hold 13 seats. Their backing could take Eisenkot's bloc to the 61-seat majority needed to form a government.However, reaching an agreement will not be easy. The main sticking point is military service exemptions traditionally granted to ultra-Orthodox seminary students. The exemptions have drawn criticism from many Israelis who believe the burden of military service is unfairly placed on the wider population.Eisenkot and his allies, particularly Lieberman, have strongly opposed these exemptions. However, Lieberman signalled some flexibility on Friday, saying he was open to a compromise."You cannot have it all", he told supporters.The two ultra-Orthodox parties have also taken different positions following the election. United Torah Judaism declined to endorse any candidate, while Shas backed Netanyahu.What happens if Eisenkot failsEisenkot has up to 42 days to form a government. If he cannot secure the necessary support, Herzog is likely to invite Netanyahu to make another attempt.Netanyahu's religious-nationalist bloc has been reduced from its original 64 seats to 53. Despite this, the prime minister could try to weaken the opposition by persuading lawmakers from rival parties to defect and join his camp.He has used this strategy before. In the run-up to the 2022 election, Netanyahu managed to destabilise the government he was opposing by drawing support away from its ranks. However, the opposition bloc at the time had a much narrower lead, meaning fewer defections were needed to bring it down.If Netanyahu gets another opportunity, he would need to find enough support to rebuild a parliamentary majority.Could a unity government emergeIf Eisenkot cannot form a government with Arab or ultra-Orthodox support, another possibility is a unity arrangement involving his Yashar party, Together, Israel Our Home and Netanyahu's Likud.Likud emerged as the largest party in the October 27 election with 27 seats. A grouping involving these parties would command 67 seats, giving it a parliamentary majority.However, this appears unlikely for now. Eisenkot and his partners would have to abandon their central campaign promise of removing Netanyahu from power. Netanyahu, in turn, would likely have to distance himself from his traditional far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies.Still, prolonged coalition negotiations or renewed fighting with Iran could push the rival camps towards a unity arrangement.Could Israel face another electionIf both Eisenkot and Netanyahu fail to form a government, parliament can nominate another candidate. The process has a deadline of around 100 days. If no candidate succeeds, Israel will have to hold another election.Herzog has already warned against another vote. On Wednesday, he said everything must be done to avoid fresh elections and urged political parties to approach consultations with an open mind.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Saudi Arabia issues danger alerts for Dammam, Dhahran and Abqaiq amid Houthi threats
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia's civil defence on Sunday issued warnings of potential danger in three eastern cities, Dammam, Dhahran and Abqaiq, amid heightened security
articles.body: Saudi Arabia's civil defence on Sunday issued warnings of potential danger in three eastern cities, Dammam, Dhahran and Abqaiq, amid heightened security concerns following a series of attacks claimed by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.The civil defence issued separate alerts for the three cities through posts on social media platform X, without specifying the nature of the potential threat. The warnings came amid continued Houthi threats and claims of attacks targeting the oil-rich kingdom.Days earlier, the Houthis had claimed responsibility for targeting Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, marking another escalation in the group's campaign against the kingdom.Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree had also claimed that the group targeted a Saudi early-warning radar system and a military transport aircraft in the kingdom's southwestern region.The latest alerts come against the backdrop of rising tensions between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed group, with the Houthis continuing to issue claims of military operations against Saudi targets.Meanwhile, Yemen has urged the Lebanese government to take coordinated and decisive action to stop Hezbollah from providing military assistance to the Houthi militia.Yemen's foreign minister Afrah Al-Zouba also backed Beirut's efforts to assert sovereign control over its territory and ensure that decisions on weapons and war remain exclusively with the Lebanese state.You use AI every day. articles.title: Watch: Shattered glass, scattered books after strong earthquake rattles Japan
articles.summary: A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured,
articles.body: A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee.The quake, which struck at 1:04 am, was located about 40 kilometres below the earth's surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.The meteorological agency warned people to brace for possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially the next two to three days.“Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall,” Ayataka Ebita, an agency official, told reporters.He said no apparent change was detected so far to the Nankai Trough plate, where scientists say a megaquake can possibly hit.The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes. Authorities frequently instruct people to stock up on bottled water, food and batteries, have plans ready to hide under tables and keep comfortable walking shoes at hand.You use AI every day. articles.title: Is Netanyahu's time up? 10 things to know as rival Gadi Eisenkot gets shot at power in Israel
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country's next government after the October 27 election failed
articles.body: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country's next government after the October 27 election failed to produce a clear parliamentary majority. It has given Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main challenger the first opportunity to take power.Eisenkot, a former chief of the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), secured recommendations from lawmakers representing 67 of the Knesset's 120 members.However, forming a coalition remains a challenge, as his bloc lacks a confirmed majority and potential partners disagree over the role of Arab parties and ultra-Orthodox factions. Netanyahu, whose Likud remains the largest party, is meanwhile pushing for a national unity government.Here are 10 things to know about the political developments in Israel.1. Eisenkot gets six weeks to form Israel's next governmentHerzog announced his decision on Saturday after consultations with representatives of political parties and separate discussions with Eisenkot and Netanyahu. The mandate gives the former military chief up to 42 days to negotiate with potential partners and secure the parliamentary support needed to form a government.The decision marks a significant setback for Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, whose attempt to retain power suffered a blow after most parliamentary factions recommended Eisenkot for the post.In his first reaction, Eisenkot called for a national emergency government. "Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," he wrote on X.2. How Eisenkot secured backing of 67 lawmakersEisenkot received recommendations from factions representing 67 lawmakers in the 120-member Knesset. These included the Jewish-led opposition bloc, which holds 48 seats, Arab party Ra'am with eight seats and the Joint List with 11 seats.The Joint List's unanimous endorsement proved crucial in taking Eisenkot past the 61-seat threshold needed for a parliamentary majority.Netanyahu, meanwhile, received recommendations from factions representing 46 lawmakers. Seven lawmakers did not endorse either candidate.However, the recommendations do not automatically translate into a governing coalition. Eisenkot must still negotiate with potential partners and secure their support on key policy issues.3. Arab parties could determine whether Eisenkot forms a governmentThe backing of Ra'am and the Joint List has given Eisenkot an important advantage. Their combined 19 seats could help him secure a majority, but working with the Arab-led parties presents a political challenge.An Arab party has been part of an Israeli governing coalition only once before. Ra'am joined the government led by former prime minister Naftali Bennett in 2021. That administration collapsed after 18 months, partly because of disagreements over the occupied West Bank.Eisenkot could form a minority government with his natural allies, including Together, The Democrats and Israel Our Home, while relying on the Arab parties for external support. Such an arrangement would give the broader grouping 67 seats.However, Avigdor Lieberman's Israel Our Home has repeatedly ruled out supporting a minority government backed by Arab parties. Only The Democrats has publicly called for their inclusion.The political sensitivities have also intensified following the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and the subsequent war in Gaza.4. Ultra-Orthodox parties offer another possible route to a majorityEisenkot and his partners could also approach Israel's two ultra-Orthodox parties, which collectively hold 13 seats. Their support could help the opposition bloc reach the 61-seat majority without relying on Arab parties.However, negotiations could run into disagreements over military service exemptions traditionally granted to ultra-Orthodox seminary students.Eisenkot and Lieberman have strongly criticised these exemptions. Many Israelis believe the arrangements place an unfair burden on other citizens who serve in the military.United Torah Judaism declined to endorse either candidate during the presidential consultations, while Shas backed Netanyahu. This leaves the possibility of an agreement open, but any deal would require difficult compromises.5. Eisenkot wants a national emergency government with four key principlesEisenkot has pitched a national emergency government to address Israel's political and security challenges. His proposed administration would be guided by four principles: recognising Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, upholding the Declaration of Independence, ensuring universal national and military conscription, and dismantling Hamas' military and political wings.His party, Yashar, has also indicated that it would only work with parties and lawmakers who accept its principles.In a statement responding to Netanyahu's appeal for a unity government, Yashar urged Likud members to distance themselves from what it described as an alliance with "radical parties", apparently referring to the far-right factions in Netanyahu's religious-nationalist bloc.6. Netanyahu loses his parliamentary majority, but Likud remains the largest partyDespite the setback, Netanyahu remains a significant force in Israeli politics. His Likud party emerged as the largest single party in the October 27 election, securing 27 seats.However, his religious-nationalist bloc has fallen from its original 64 seats to 53, leaving it short of the 61 required for a parliamentary majority.The prime minister also suffered a setback when United Torah Judaism refused to endorse him during consultations with Herzog. The party's decision has raised questions about the stability of his long-standing political alliance with ultra-Orthodox factions.7. Netanyahu calls for a national unity government to counter Eisenkot's bidFollowing Eisenkot's appointment, Netanyahu called for the immediate formation of a broad national unity government comprising all Zionist political factions.In a televised address, he argued that Israel needed a united political leadership to address external security threats, particularly from Iran.The proposed government, Netanyahu said, would "permanently remove the nuclear threat from Iran, preserve Israel as a Jewish state, and bring unity among us".However, the opposition rejected his appeal. Democratic Party chairman Yair Golan said Netanyahu's government must be replaced by a "government of salvation and change" to protect Israel's democracy, security and future.Golan also called for ultra-Orthodox citizens to be conscripted into the military and integrated into the workforce. He argued that the burden of defence and taxation should not fall disproportionately on secular Israelis.8. Netanyahu seeks to prevent Eisenkot from joining hands with Arab partiesA key part of Netanyahu's political strategy has been to discourage any arrangement between Eisenkot and the Arab-led parties.He has repeatedly portrayed their participation in government as a national security threat. Shortly before Herzog announced his decision, Netanyahu warned against "hastily swearing in a government with terrorist supporters", a description he uses for the Arab-led parties.He has also made unsubstantiated claims that Arab parties "stole" the elections.Eisenkot, meanwhile, has indicated that he could work with them under certain conditions, including their acceptance of his position that Hamas is a terrorist organisation that must be destroyed.The issue could become one of the biggest obstacles in Eisenkot's efforts to form a government.9. Netanyahu could get another opportunity if Eisenkot failsIf Eisenkot fails to form a government within 42 days, Herzog could give Netanyahu the next opportunity to secure a parliamentary majority.The prime minister could attempt to weaken the opposition by persuading lawmakers from rival parties to defect and join his camp.Netanyahu has used similar political manoeuvres in the past. In the run-up to the 2022 election, he managed to destabilise the coalition opposing him and eventually returned to power.However, his current challenge is more difficult because the opposition bloc has a wider base of support and he would need to attract a greater number of lawmakers to secure a majority.10. Another election remains possible if both leaders failIf neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu succeeds in forming a government, the Knesset could nominate another candidate to attempt the task.The process has a deadline of around 100 days. If no candidate manages to form a government within that period, Israel would have to hold another election.A unity government between Eisenkot's partners and Netanyahu's Likud is another possible outcome, although it appears unlikely at present. Such an arrangement would command 67 seats, but Eisenkot's allies would have to abandon their central electoral promise of removing Netanyahu from power. Netanyahu, in turn, would have to distance himself from his far-right and ultra-Orthodox political allies.Herzog has urged political parties to approach negotiations with an open mind and do everything possible to avoid another election.You use AI every day. articles.title: An elderly man fell while carrying breakfast and severed an artery; two Queensland carpenters used a dress and adhesive tape to save his life, leaving his wife overwhelmed with gratitude
articles.summary: An ordinary morning in Gracemere, Queensland, turned into a life-threatening emergency when 93-year-old Ian Barton suffered a severe wrist injury after
articles.body: An ordinary morning in Gracemere, Queensland, turned into a life-threatening emergency when 93-year-old Ian Barton suffered a severe wrist injury after falling while carrying a bowl of porridge. The bowl shattered during the fall, and a fragment sliced an artery in his wrist, causing heavy bleeding. Hearing a woman screaming for help from across the street, carpenter Josh Sander and his apprentice Gary Tunbridge abandoned their work and rushed to assist him. When a tea towel failed to control the bleeding, the two men improvised a tighter dressing using a dress and adhesive tape from their work vehicle. They continued applying pressure while waiting approximately 40 minutes for an ambulance. Barton was eventually taken to hospital, where he underwent surgery and remained in a stable condition.A morning job turns into a life-threatening emergencyThe incident occurred shortly before 8am on Monday, November 2, 2026, in a quiet cul-de-sac in Gracemere, a town near Rockhampton in central Queensland, Australia.Sander and Tunbridge were working on a pergola at a nearby property and were preparing to climb onto its roof when they heard a woman screaming for help from across the street.The woman was Joy Barton, 89, whose husband, Ian, had fallen in their backyard. The two tradesmen immediately stopped working and rushed to the property.They found the 93-year-old lying on his back patio, surrounded by blood. According to Sander's account to ABC Capricornia, Barton had tripped over the raised edge of a small ramp while carrying his breakfast. He fell onto the bowl of porridge, which shattered and caused a deep cut to his wrist.Sander initially paused when he saw the amount of blood but quickly realised that the injury had severed an artery and that the situation was potentially life-threatening."We just ripped in and weren't afraid to get a bit bloody and it's turned out for the best," Sander told ABC.Two carpenters use a dress and adhesive tape to control bleedingSander initially attempted to control the bleeding by wrapping a tea towel tightly around Barton's injured wrist. However, it did not slow the blood loss sufficiently.Realising that they needed a tighter dressing, he asked Tunbridge to retrieve adhesive tape from their work truck. Sander then went inside the house and found one of Joy Barton's dresses.The two men used the dress fabric to wrap the wound, after which Tunbridge tightly secured it with adhesive tape. They also continued applying pressure to the injury and the makeshift tourniquet in an effort to control the bleeding.Sander explained that the first attempt with the tea towel had not been sufficient, prompting him to look for something that could provide a tighter wrap.The improvised dressing became central to their efforts to keep Barton alive until emergency services arrived.Elderly man repeatedly loses consciousness during ambulance waitThe two tradesmen remained with Barton for approximately 40 minutes before paramedics reached the property.The situation remained serious throughout the wait. Sander said Barton repeatedly appeared to fade away, forcing the men to try to wake him and keep him responsive.At one point, they noticed that the elderly man appeared to be choking. Tunbridge realised that Barton's false teeth were lodged in his mouth and reached in to remove them to help keep his airway clear.Sander later recalled that his apprentice had acted quickly after noticing the problem, helping maintain the man's airflow while they waited for medical assistance.A Queensland Ambulance Service spokesperson told ABC that the local Gracemere crew was experiencing significant demand at the time but responded as quickly as possible to treat and transport the patient to hospital.The service also thanked members of the community for their quick thinking and for providing care before paramedics arrived.93-year-old undergoes surgery at Rockhampton HospitalBarton was taken to Rockhampton Hospital for treatment of his serious wrist injury. He remained in a stable condition and underwent an operation on the afternoon of the incident.His wife, Joy, later described how frightened she had been when she saw her husband being taken away by paramedics.She recalled kissing him as he was placed on the ambulance chair because she feared he might not survive.However, she was relieved to see a considerable improvement in his appearance after the operation.The family was hopeful that Barton would be able to return home within the following days. Joy said he would likely need several months of recovery at home after leaving hospital.Wife thanks tradesmen for saving her husband's lifeJoy expressed deep gratitude to Sander and Tunbridge for responding to the emergency and helping her husband before the ambulance arrived.She said she believed the two men had saved Ian's life and described them as heroes."They saved my husband's life ... I thought he was going to die," she told ABC.Joy also recalled telling her husband after his operation: "Ian, darling, that bloke saved your life."The couple have been married for more than six decades, making the incident particularly frightening for their family.Their granddaughter posted a message on social media the following day, thanking the tradesmen for helping her grandfather. The post helped bring attention to their actions and allowed the family to identify and publicly acknowledge the two men.Joy said she was still trying to work out how she could repay them for what they had done. Sander and Tunbridge, meanwhile, said they were simply relieved that Barton was recovering.Apprentice had started his carpentry career four months earlierThe incident was particularly remarkable for Tunbridge, who had begun his carpentry apprenticeship only four months before the emergency.Despite being relatively new to the trade, he worked alongside Sander to help Barton during the critical wait for medical assistance.When asked about the possibility of becoming a paramedic after the experience, Tunbridge joked that emergency medical work had not been part of his apprenticeship training and that he had no immediate plans to change careers.Sander also reflected on his first-aid knowledge, admitting that it had been several years since he last completed a first-aid course. The experience prompted him to consider booking a refresher course.The two tradesmen had been focused on an ordinary construction job that morning before the emergency across the street brought their work to an unexpected halt.You use AI every day. articles.title: Houthi attacks target Aramco facilities in Saudi Arabia as explosions rock Riyadh
articles.summary: Multiple loud explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh after the country's Civil Defence issued an early-warning alert over a potential
articles.body: Multiple loud explosions were heard in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh after the country's Civil Defence issued an early-warning alert over a potential threat.Witnesses as per Reuters reported damage to a building belonging to oil giant Saudi Aramco in the city's financial district amid renewed hostilities with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels.A Reuters witness reported hearing several loud booms shortly after the alert was issued. The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles over Riyadh and the southern region. It also said two Houthi missiles fired towards the capital had been intercepted.Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for a series of missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi oil facilities and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. He said six military operations had been carried out against strategic and military installations across the kingdom using ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones.According to Saree, the attacks were launched in response to what the group described as Saudi aggression against Yemen."The first operation targeted Khalid International Airport, oil storage tanks, and a distillation tower belonging to Aramco in the Saudi enemy's capital, Riyadh, and, by Allah's grace, successfully achieved its objective," Saree said.He said the second operation targeted Aramco facilities in Khurais, while the third struck Pumping Station No. 8 in the Dawadmi area.The fourth operation, according to the spokesperson, targeted Saudi military concentrations at a National Guard camp in Najran. The fifth targeted troop positions east of Al-Jawf Governorate in three stages."The sixth operation targeted Saudi enemy troop concentrations east of Raghwah and Madghal districts in Marib Governorate, under the command of Saudi officer Fares Al-Shammari, leaving a large number of dead and wounded among their ranks," he added.Saree claimed that the operations caused several casualties among Saudi military personnel. These claims have not been independently verified.In a separate post on X, the Houthi spokesperson alleged that Saudi Arabia had carried out 105 airstrikes and missile attacks on Yemen over the preceding 24 hours, targeting areas in Sanaa and the governorates of Al-Jawf, Taiz, Amran, Hajjah, Saada, Marib and Lahj."These attacks left dozens of civilians dead and wounded, most of them women and children. This brings the total number of airstrikes and missile attacks by the Saudi aggressor against our country since the escalation began to 4,369," he said.Threatening further retaliation, Saree said, "We will continue our operations deep inside Saudi territory, imposing the equation of blockade for blockade and escalation for escalation, and targeting Saudi enemy troop concentrations and officers."Meanwhile, Yemen's internationally recognised government has urged Lebanon to take coordinated measures to stop Hezbollah's alleged military assistance to the Houthi militia.Yemen's Foreign Minister Afrah Al-Zouba called for cooperation between the security and intelligence agencies of the two countries to prevent further support for Houthi military operations.The renewed fighting has shattered a United Nations-brokered truce reached in 2022, which had largely halted attacks between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis, who control Sanaa. The group has since resumed missile and drone attacks targeting Saudi airports and oil facilities, while Riyadh has carried out airstrikes in Yemen in support of its Yemeni allies.The escalation, linked to the wider US-Iran conflict, has revived the 12-year war in Yemen, which has triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises and left the Arab world's poorest country deeply fragmented.The International Organization for Migration said in October that more than 200,000 people had been displaced since the latest round of fighting began.You use AI every day. articles.title: BJP chief Nitin Nabin asks opposition to follow LK Advani's approach to national security
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday urged opposition parties to learn from veteran leader and former deputy prime minister L K Advani, saying
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday urged opposition parties to learn from veteran leader and former deputy prime minister L K Advani, saying political parties should stand together with the government whenever the country faces a challenge related to national security.Speaking at a special event at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi to mark Advani's 100th birthday, Nabin recalled the veteran leader's stand in Parliament when the BJP was in the Opposition.“Whenever he spoke in Parliament, he always said that the BJP will be with the government on issues related to the country's security despite being in the Opposition. As a Leader of the Opposition, he said very clearly that the entire Opposition would be with the government when it came to the country. This is something people need to learn even today,” Nabin said.He described Advani as an inspiration for BJP workers and said his commitment to the nation-first ideology had helped shape the party's growth.Nabin recalls Advani's partnership with VajpayeeNabin said Advani and former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee had different temperaments and personalities, but their ability to work together towards a common goal was unparalleled.He credited the two leaders with laying the foundation for the BJP's expansion from a party with just two Lok Sabha MPs, saying their determination helped the organisation overcome uncertainty in its early years.“As India moves forward into the 21st century, the Bharatiya Janata Party is also moving ahead with its expansion and development. The BJP is working to take forward both the heritage of this country and the legacy of the party,” he said.Nabin also described Advani as an example of the dignity, probity and sensitivity that politics should uphold.“I could not get an opportunity to work with him, but what I have heard from others who worked with him tells me that Advani's life has been an inspiration for everyone in BJP,” he said.He added that Advani had demonstrated immense dedication to the nation despite having experienced the pain of Partition.“He could take even hard decisions with simplicity,” Nabin said.Ram Rath Yatra and Ayodhya temple recalledRecalling Advani's role in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, Nabin referred to the veteran leader's Ram Rath Yatra, which was stopped at Samastipur in Bihar.He said the slogan “We will build the temple right there” had been raised by BJP workers and crores of people across the country. Although the yatra was halted in Bihar, kar sevaks carried forward Advani's mission, he said.Nabin credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi with taking that journey forward, pointing to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya as a moment to remember Advani's contribution.“Today, as the country witnesses the magnificent Shri Ram Temple standing in Ayodhya, it is a moment for all of us to honour and remember Shri Advani Ji's historic journey,” he said.Piyush Goyal recalls personal associationSenior Union minister and BJP treasurer Piyush Goyal also recalled his association with Advani, saying the veteran leader never made others feel the weight of his seniority or influence.He said party workers fondly called Advani 'dada' and that the leader had always treated him like a family member, addressing him by his nickname, 'Happy'.“Advani only thought about taking the country and taking the party forward with complete selflessness,” Goyal said, while wishing him a long life.“We all wish that this country continues to get a leader like Lal Krishna Advani,” he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
